# Ex-Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon says he's 90% certain China has spies inside America's AI giants

Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon says he is 90% certain that Chinese spies have infiltrated two of America's leading artificial intelligence companies, warning that Beijing could steal technological breakthroughs regardless of whether U.S. developers slow their progress.

Coxon made the allegation during an interview with entrepreneur Patrick Bet-David on the PBD Podcast , arguing that the possibility of espionage undermines the idea that the United States can maintain its lead in artificial intelligence by controlling the pace of domestic development.

"I think one really important thing people don't realize is that China already has spies at OpenAI and Anthropic," adding that he's 90% positive. "It's almost certain that they have spies already there … There's no serious background check for this sort of stuff yet."

## Coxon says China could steal America's AI advances at any moment

Coxon's allegations about Chinese espionage follow his departure from Anthropic, where he has said he became increasingly concerned about the direction of AI development.

The claim also comes as conversation continues surrounding whether or not companies developing increasingly powerful systems — systems that Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei believes could go so far as curing cancer — can innovate at a responsible pace and adequately protect their technology.

Policymakers are actively debating whether the United States should accelerate AI development to maintain its competitive advantage over China or introduce stronger safeguards to address potential risks.

But Coxton's latest comments add another dimension to that debate: whether the United States can meaningfully control the risks associated with AI development if sensitive advances can be obtained by foreign competitors already.

During the podcast interview, Coxon argued that, even if American AI companies pull ahead of Chinese competitors, the advantage may not last — because research and technological breakthroughs can be stolen.

"China has the ability to hack at any time," he said. "If we pull ahead, that doesn't give us a big lead. They can just step in, steal our progress at any time and catch up."

On the contrary, if the United States slows down, he believes it could also slow down China.

"If we slow down, it will probably slow down China quite a bit, too, because, currently, a lot of their progress is from essentially copying or stealing U.S. work — not all of it, but there is a component," Coxton said.

## Former researcher has long warned about AI safety

Coxon neither named names nor provided evidence to substantiate his allegation, and his comments do not establish that Chinese intelligence operatives are working inside either company. But, he's not alone in his train of thinking amid the mounting doomsday narrative surrounding the national security implications of advanced AI and the intensifying competition between the United States and China.

Coxon resigned from Anthropic in September and has since publicly warned that the race to develop increasingly capable AI systems could create serious risks if companies prioritize technological advancement over safety.

In his resignation announcement on X , Coxon wrote: "I resigned from Anthropic today. I spent the last three years doing pre-training research at both OpenAI and Anthropic. Neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives."

In the podcast, Coxon continued that the technology's implications extend beyond ordinary commercial competition, describing AI as a potential national security threat.

"This is a super weapon," he said. "So soon people are going to have to realize that this is not like a casual business thing."
